docs.title: Frame and Position Parameters
docs.text:
Set the frames and the mounting position on the device; Native ROS 2 has no ROS parameters. Use the CoLa telegrams below, the REST endpoint of the same name, or the web interface.

Frame and Position Parameters: parameter, CoLa telegram, and effect.

Parameter CoLa telegram Effect Frame ID sWN rosFrameId header.frame_id of the published messages Parent frame ID sWN rosParentFrameId Parent frame of the sensor transform, for example world Namespace sWN rosNamespace Prepended to all topic names; empty for no namespace Sensor position sWN SensorPosition Mounting position (x, y, z in mm) and orientation (yaw, pitch, roll in 1/10000°), published as a transform on /tf Domain ID sWN rosDomainId ROS 2 domain ID (0-232); must match ROS_DOMAIN_ID on the host

For the telegram structures and examples, see the CoLa Telegram Listings of the multiScan200 and the picoScan100. After changing the static IP address, restart the device so that the topics are published correctly.

docs.title: DDS Capabilities
docs.text:
Because the device runs a DDS participant in its firmware, it joins the ROS 2 network as a first-class peer:

  • Interoperability: ROS 2 nodes, MathWorks ROS Toolbox, OpenDDS-based systems, and custom DDS clients can subscribe directly.
  • Multiple subscribers: The sensor publishes once per scan; adding subscribers does not add another device-side publishing step.
  • Per-subscriber QoS: Subscribers can negotiate policies independently, such as BEST_EFFORT for control and RELIABLE for recording.
  • Automatic discovery: RTPS discovery finds subscribers without a broker or static IP table.
  • Hardware timestamps: header.stamp is set at the hardware scan trigger. With PTP synchronization, it aligns with other sensors.

docs.title: sick_scan_xd
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 picoScan100

The sick_scan_xd driver runs as a ROS 1 or ROS 2 node on the host. It receives sensor data, assembles complete scans, and publishes ROS messages. Choose this approach when you need host-side decoding control, IMU data on ROS topics where supported, or integration with a device that has no native publisher. It also supports recording and playback with rosbag .db3 files. The driver is available from the sick_scan_xd GitHub repository.

docs.title: CPU Load Comparison
docs.text:
Measurements across 11 picoScan150 profiles used 15-50 Hz scan rates, 0.05-1.0° angular resolutions, 100 scans per method, and IEEE 1588 PTP synchronization. Single-echo sensor_msgs/LaserScan data was used for a direct comparison.

CPU Load Comparison: parameter and value.

Parameter Value Host Raspberry Pi 4, ARM Cortex-A72, 4 cores, Ubuntu 22.04 RMW Fast DDS (rmw_fastrtps_cpp) Network Direct Gigabit Ethernet Latency definition Δt = treceive_on_host − header.stamp

Average system CPU load was 8.5% for native ROS 2 and 21.5% for sick_scan_xd, expressed as the percentage of one Raspberry Pi 4 CPU core.

docs.title: Set Time Stamp [sMN LSPsetdatetime]
docs.text:
The data format in the telegram is: +2009{SPC}+7{SPC}+22{SPC}+12{SPC}+0{SPC}+0{SPC}+0.The numbers represent year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond.

If plus is used up-front the data it is interpreted as an integer decimal number, without the plus it's the scanner reads the data as hex format.

The answer is always in ASCII format.

Does only work if NTP- respectively PTP-Client is not active.

There is no real time clock inside the device. When the scanner is switched off and after a reboot, the time has to be set again. Therefore, it is recommended to use a NTP or a PTP setting.

docs.title: Set Angle Range Filter [sWN LFPangleRangeFilter]
docs.text:
The angle range Horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) limits in units of 1/10000 degree.

BeamIncrement = the 'beamIncrement' which is used to subsample the beams within the selected angle range. With a 'beamIncrement' of n only every nth beam from the selected angle range is copied to the output scan, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. If the beamIncrement is zero it is set to one.

docs.title: SOPASair Walkthrough
docs.text:
SOPASair is the built-in web interface of the multiScan100 for parameterization, service, and diagnostics. It runs directly on the sensor, so no software installation is needed. Connect the sensor to the same network as your computer and open http://<sensor-ip>/ in a browser. The factory default address is 192.168.0.1.

You can view status and settings without logging in. To change settings, log in with the Authorized Client user level using the user icon in the top bar.

The SOPASair Home dashboard: device status, 3D live view with field evaluation, input and output states, and detection history at a glance.

docs.title: Home
docs.text:
The Home page summarizes the sensor's state. It is a good place to start before you change any settings.

Status shows separate indicators for the device, connection, measurement, field evaluation, and data output. Because each state is reported independently, the sensor can be measuring while no data is sent to an external receiver.

Device and application status indicators.

Device information lists the model, part number, serial number, firmware version, system time, and the time of the last save. Check the firmware version before you use a firmware-specific API example. Click Find device to make the sensor LEDs blink, so you can identify the unit on site.

Device identity and installed firmware version.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The Configuration menu contains the measurement, filter, mounting, network, and I/O settings. For the matching REST parameters, value ranges, and variant-specific limits, see the multiScan100 OpenAPI reference.

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text:
Configuration > Basic settings contains interlaced mode, the status LED, and the measurement state.

Interlaced mode, LED, and measurement settings.

Date and system time shows the device clock and its synchronization source. Apply computer time sets the sensor clock to your computer's time. For network-based time sources, see Time synchronization.

Device clock and time synchronization settings.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
Configuration > Filter combines the fog, echo, particle, and moving-average filters. The echo filter selects all, first, or last echoes, and the moving-average filter sets the averaging depth. See Filter details to choose the right filters for your application.

Fog, echo, particle, and moving-average filters.

docs.title: Mounting
docs.text:
Configuration > Mounting describes how the sensor is installed. Select a preset mounting position or enter the orientation angles and position offsets. Adjust fields to mounting position moves existing fields to match the new mounting, and Accept IMU data takes the orientation from the internal IMU.

Mounting position, orientation, and offsets.

The Inertial measuring unit (IMU) panel shows the current orientation and acceleration. Because the IMU is not calibrated, use its values as a starting point for the mounting orientation, not as a precise measurement.

IMU orientation and acceleration.

docs.title: Contamination Indication
docs.text:
Configuration > Contamination indication monitors the front window for dirt. The sector diagram shows the contamination state per sector, using the color legend below it. You can configure whether a warning or error is output, the sensitivity, the monitored sectors, the handling of blocked sectors, and the response delay. See Contamination indication for the application background.

Contamination status per sector and evaluation settings.

docs.title: Connection Options
docs.text:
Configuration > Connection options contains the Ethernet settings: addressing mode, IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, MAC address, and link speed.

When you click Apply, the new network settings take effect immediately. The browser loses its connection if the sensor moves to an address that your computer cannot reach, so note the new address before applying the change.

Ethernet addressing and link settings.

docs.title: Inputs and Outputs
docs.text:
Configuration > Inputs and outputs assigns each port a name and a direction. For outputs, select the signal source, inversion, logic, and restart behavior. The connector diagram next to each port shows the corresponding pin. The status panels below show the current input and output states, and Reset counters clears the output switching counters.

Port assignments with connector pin diagrams.

docs.title: Applications
docs.text: The Applications menu contains measurement-data output and field evaluation. Some variants offer additional functions. For example, the multiScan165S with Safe 3D Object Detection adds a ground filter and perpendicular distance measurement as non-safety-related functions.

docs.title: Data Output
docs.text:
Application > Data output selects the measurement-data format, MSGPACK or Compact, and the UDP destination address and port. Start or stop the data stream from the same panel. See Data streaming to choose a receiver and parser.

Output format, UDP destination, and stream control.

IMU data is streamed separately, with its own destination address, port, and start/stop control.

IMU data output.

Data reduction limits the output by scan layer, angular range, and output interval. Range filter removes points outside a cuboid area or a distance window. If layers or points are missing from the received data, check these settings together with the output format.

Scan-layer, angular-range, and interval reduction.

Cuboid-area and distance filters.

docs.title: Field Evaluation
docs.text:
Application > Field evaluation monitors fields for objects and switches outputs when a field is infringed. Each group combines fields, evaluations, and outputs, and has its own activation source. Resource requirements shows how much of the sensor's evaluation capacity is in use, and Detection list shows recent detections.

Evaluation groups with their activation sources.

See Field evaluation for a complete commissioning procedure and API support.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Diagnostics > Overview combines status, device information, operating information, the current device status, and the message log. Expand Operating information to see the number of power-on cycles, the operating hours, and the time of the last parameterization.

Power-on count, operating hours, and last parameterization.

The message table lists current and past events with their status, number, time, description, and counter. Current device status shows only the messages that are still active. If you need support, use Create diagnostic file to collect the device state in one file and send it to SICK. See Contact.

docs.title: Cybersecurity
docs.text:
Diagnostics > Cybersecurity shows the HTTPS certificates and the Services and protocols table. The table lists each service with its purpose and port, so you can enable only the services your integration needs. See HTTPS and certificates for the complete certificate setup.

Services and protocols with their ports.

docs.title: Data Recorder
docs.text:
Diagnostics > Data recorder explains how to install the SICK data recorder on your computer and connect it to the sensor. Use the recorder to capture measurement data for later analysis or support cases.

Installation and connection steps for the data recorder.

docs.title: Detection History
docs.text:
Diagnostics > Detection history records field-evaluation detections. Select the evaluations to include, then start the history. The Statistics section counts the detections per evaluation, and the Detection list shows each event with its time stamp. Use Reset detection history to clear the counters.

Detection counts per evaluation.

docs.title: Release Notes
docs.text: This page summarizes firmware changes for the multiScan100 product family from firmware version 2.x.x. Check the release and device variant before updating or using a feature.

docs.title: General Information
docs.text:
• Firmware 2.x.x is the standard firmware for all multiScan100 variants.
  • multiScan100-S has a separate firmware file, which must be requested.
  • A firmware update typically does not affect active parameter settings.
  • Purchased licenses are not affected by firmware upgrades.
  • Reboot the device after activating or deactivating licenses.

docs.title: Update Instructions
docs.text:
Update via SOPAS ET.

multiScan100 firmware can be updated through SOPAS ET, Sentio Creator, or the web UI (SOPASair). The update uses an .spk software package. The procedure below uses SOPAS ET.

  1. Download and unpack the firmware package from the relevant product's download section on sick.com.
  2. Connect the multiScan100 to the computer over Ethernet and ensure that it is booted. Keep the power supply stable during the update.
  3. Find the sensor in SOPAS ET and add it to the project.
  4. Save the parameter file (.sopas) as a precaution. Read parameters from the device to synchronize the project, then export the configuration.
  5. Open the device settings, choose Download firmware, select the .spk package, and start the update.
  6. Log in at the Service user level.
  7. Wait for the update and reboot to complete and for the device LED to turn green. Check the firmware version in SOPAS ET; reinstall the device driver if prompted.
  8. Before operating the device, verify that it works as expected and that its parameters are set as intended.

If the device state is unclear after the update, load factory defaults at the Service user level and then load the saved parameter file.

Update via SOPASair.

Firmware updates through SOPASair in a web browser are supported from version 2.4.1. Use the signed .spk.signed package. Start the update from the device menu or from the link on the displayed firmware version.

docs.title: Firmware 2.4.4
docs.text:
Release date: 5 May 2026. Firmware 2.4.3 was not released.

New features.

  • Firmware 2.4.4 is available for multiScan165S. The previous firmware for that variant is 2.3.0.
  • Ground Filter and Perpendicular Distance are available as non-safety-related add-ons for multiScan165S with Safe 3D Object Detection (part number 1151596). See the current multiScan165S operating instructions for details.

Optimization.

The FPGA version was updated for production optimization. Firmware 2.4.4 is functionally identical to 2.4.2.

Known issues.

Contamination-indication sectors may not be saved permanently and can be lost after a reboot.

As a workaround, import an appropriate sensor configuration after reboot and verify the sector setup. Use the REST /ContaminationConfig endpoint or the CoLa A/B sWN ContaminationConfig telegram for parameterization.

docs.title: Firmware 2.4.2
docs.text:
Release date: 20 October 2025

New features.

Firmware 2.4.2 adds support for multiScan166. Earlier firmware versions do not support multiScan166.

docs.title: Firmware 2.4.1
docs.text:
Release date: 20 October 2025

New features.

Ground Filter.

The Ground Filter provides upper and lower ground-threshold values. In applications with moving objects, it can reduce false field-evaluation triggers caused by the ground. When configured correctly, it is intended to retain detection of small objects such as forklift tines. The filter can be used indoors and outdoors. It affects both field evaluation and Perpendicular Distance.

Perpendicular Distance.

For an object inside a configured box-shaped field, Perpendicular Distance can output the object's minimum and maximum distance to an axis (X, Y, or Z). Use sRN perpendicularDistanceResult for a one-time request and sEN perpendicularDistanceResult for event-based output.

Firmware update via web GUI.

Firmware can be updated through the web GUI without SOPAS ET, using the signed .spk.signed package.

Parameter import and export.

The firmware adds parameter import and export through the web GUI.

GUI optimization and feature enhancements.

  • The multiScan-S is shown with a yellow ring in the GUI.
  • Field contours uploaded by telegram are transferred directly to the web UI.
  • The Cybersecurity overview shows that the Maintenance and Authorized Client user levels are disabled by default. They can be enabled in the GUI after logging in at the Service user level.
  • HTTPS is supported for multiScan100 GUI components.
  • Full-screen mode can be selected by adding ?fullscreen_mode= to the scan view URL.
  • The web update file dialog allows only signed .spk files.
  • The scan-layer filter has a redesigned interface and allows individual layers to be deactivated.
  • The distance filter displays minimum- and maximum-distance spheres to show the selected area.
  • An Undo button was added next to Save.
  • The Fullscreen button was moved from the top line next to split view to the device menu.
  • The DHCP fallback mode was changed to Static IP.
  • The GetFieldEvaluationContour telegram was implemented.

Temperature improvements.

The temperature range was extended from +50 °C to +60 °C when the device is mounted with standard bracket 2130373. The device does not shut off when its temperature exceeds the configured limits.

Firmware 2.4.1: usage condition and mission time.

Usage condition Mission time Continuous use at 25 °C 42 years Continuous use rarely above 30 °C 37.5 years 55% of the time up to 30 °C, 35% up to 40 °C, and 10% up to 50 °C 20 years 70% of the time up to 30 °C and 30% up to 50 °C 18 years 80% of the time up to 30 °C and 20% up to 60 °C 13.4 years Continuous use at 50 °C 8 years

When a configured temperature range is exceeded, an output can be switched. Use these telegrams for temperature warnings:

  • Read current device temperature alarm status: sRN temperatureAlarmStatus
  • Set device temperature alarm configuration: sWN temperatureAlarmConfiguration
  • Read device temperature alarm configuration: sRN temperatureAlarmConfiguration

Bug fixes.

  • Harmonized sensor behavior with other LiDAR sensors.
  • Fixed diagnostic dumps not downloading through the GUI.
  • Fixed measurement data sometimes not appearing in the UI after a browser refresh.
  • Fixed an error when creating fields with X/Y extents greater than 100 m.
  • Fixed missing layer selection in the Object Detection scheme.
  • Fixed the queue-overflow error not resetting when streaming was stopped while the error was active.

docs.title: Firmware 2.3.0
docs.text:
Release date: 2 December 2024

New features.

  • High-resolution layers in 3D Object Detection: Choose among 14 one-degree scan layers or either of two high-resolution layers (2D scan layers 6 or 14). A field can be configured multiple times with different sources. multiScan165 does not have high-resolution layers.
  • Detection History: The 3D Object Detection software adds a page for reviewing field-infringement history and logs of current field status.
  • REST firmware update: Firmware updates can be performed using REST.
  • Online Help: Existing help was updated with new content and guidance.
  • I/O application: Adds a warning when I/O ports cannot be created and removes FieldEvaluationAppState from the source list.
  • CoLa1 password handling: ROM passwords were removed; only RAM passwords are permitted.
  • Third-party components: Updated to newer versions.
  • GUI changes: Input configuration is visible when Port 1 is set to Input; the start page can show field evaluation or measurement data; the Field Evaluation Scan GUI can receive scan layers (for multiScan136, both one-degree and high-resolution layers); and the I/O status display was redesigned.

Bug fixes and improvements.

  • IMU errors, including missing data delivery, now generate an error notification.
  • Fixed mounting position not being written when set in the SOPAS ET device window.
  • Fixed the error when connecting more than 20 sources to an output.
  • PTP is no longer shown in the selection list when no PTP license is available.
  • Switching between streaming and field-evaluation views is disabled when either required license is missing.
  • System Diagnosis displays the sensor's local time when configured, instead of UTC.
  • Corrected the translation of “No echo” to “Ignore missing echo.”
  • Duplicated evaluations appear in the GUI without reloading the browser.
  • Fixed the maximum-range circle being tilted; it is positioned in the scanner's zero-degree layer.
  • Fixed the preset mounting position not being displayed correctly.
  • Field-evaluation response-time frames now reflect the scanning frequency.
  • Online Help no longer overlaps the settings area.
  • Fixed an Access Denied error when rapidly clicking + in Object Detection.
  • White points are visible in Echo View.
  • Fixed CoLa 2 reading and writing of Port Configuration and Source List.
  • Fixed deserialization of Compact azimuth angles above pi.
  • Cleaned up different API interfaces.

Known issues.

Hardware.

At startup, the motor may not begin rotating immediately and a Motor Stalled error may appear in the error log. The sensorless motor driver cannot measure the current frequency at startup. It retries its start sequence, which may take up to six seconds; after ten seconds, software resets the driver module.

Firmware.

  • DoDiagnosis increases system load and can adversely affect measurement operation, potentially causing additional errors.
  • While the GUI creates a diagnostic file, the device LED can remain green and the status can show READY even though 3D Object Detection and field evaluation are blocked. Normal operation resumes when file generation is complete.
  • Ports configured as inputs with a 5-pin system plug do not work with Active Low.

Application and UI.

  • In the Upper Z limit field, the cursor can jump vertically when the field is empty; this does not occur when it contains text.
  • Device-name assignment can produce an error.
  • A soft reset triggered through the UI can cause web-server error messages.
  • Creating fields with an X/Y extent greater than 100 m can cause an error and prevent field evaluation from working.
  • The queue-overflow error is not reset when streaming stops while the error is active.
  • Layer selection is missing in the Object Detection scheme.
  • Duplicating evaluations can fail after a group and evaluation are created, one evaluation is duplicated, and the original is deleted. Adding a new evaluation with ID 1 allows duplication again.

docs.title: Firmware 2.2.2
docs.text:
Compatible with: multiScan100; Release date: 19 August 2024

New features.

Licensed 3D Object Detection for multiScan165.

The licensed SensorApp was already available for multiScan136. For multiScan165, it supports collision avoidance and area monitoring, with up to 48 configurable fields. The evaluation uses real elevation angles based on each sensor's production calibration data. It improves evaluation of object position and size for multiScan136 and multiScan165, using all 16 layers for multiScan165.

More simultaneously active fields require more processing and increase system load. Excessive load can cause performance problems or system errors. Deactivating other features, such as the GUI, measurement-data output, and filters, can reduce load and allow more fields to be active.

  • Additional GUI languages were added.
  • An internal recorder can record and play back data on the device; a separate recorder tool is required.
  • sRN FieldEvaluationGroupState reads evaluation-group state: 0 = not configured, 1 = active, 2 = inactive.
  • Online Help was updated.
  • Scan-GUI visualization was optimized, including use of scanner-specific elevation angles.
  • The GUI now warns when an object is too small compared with the layer distance.
  • Support for multiScan165 was added.

Fixes, improvements, and changes.

  • Improved port selection in 3D Object Detection; ports already in use are no longer selectable.
  • Improved resource monitoring in 3D Object Detection. Warnings indicate potential high load and help identify which functions use resources; creating additional fields no longer produces an error message, only warnings.
  • Applied performance optimizations and improved the GUI structure.
  • Aligned contamination-indication and warning-LED behavior.
  • Improved 3D Object Detection field visualization. Fixed field duplication being limited to four consecutive duplications and group deletion not working correctly.
  • Fixed system time not being applied or displayed correctly.
  • Mounting settings are visible without an IMU license.
  • Improved contamination-indication timing and error handling.
  • Fixed deleted 3D Object Detection field points remaining in the GUI.
  • Corrected display of umlauts in the Input/Output window.
  • Reduced the internally blocked 169.254.x.x IP address range.
  • Fixed the reset and maintenance communication-interface function.
  • System timestamps, including IMU, 3D Object Detection, and scan timestamps, are in UTC.
  • The interval filter now starts at 2.
  • Removed the sensitivity setting from Inputs/Outputs (edge/level).
  • When more than three echoes are measured, the last echo is used instead of the third.
  • An application-state error now changes the device state to error.
  • Queue-overflow errors are shown only when data loss occurs.

Known issues.

  • More than 100 field points can produce a duplicate error message.
  • In Object Detection, quickly clicking + after opening the page can produce Access Denied (/api/EvaluationGroupMapping).
  • Duplicating fields may not work correctly. Press F5 to refresh the browser as a workaround.
  • GUI CPU usage can increase over time. If the GUI freezes, close and reopen the browser.
  • Connecting more than 20 sources to an output produces an error.
  • The change-password dialog may not disappear.
  • An incorrect error message is shown if polygon points exceed 100 m.
  • The queue-overflow error is not reset when streaming stops while the error is active.

Firmware hash.

The published SHA-256 hash for the firmware file is:

110a4eb514b7ec868ecd97f2fc40ec8418dd5e5f56a7e48a099d649e3a84e2b6

Compare a downloaded file's SHA-256 fingerprint with the value published by SICK to check that the file has not been corrupted or manipulated.

Chrome 128 scan-view issue.

During tests with the Chrome 128 beta, measurement data was not displayed in the 2D and 3D SOPASair visualizations. SOPAS ET was not affected. Microsoft Edge was also affected because it uses the same software base.

Workarounds are to update the sensor to the latest firmware, use Firefox, use SOPAS ET, or use Chrome Portable version 127 or earlier. Firmware 2.2.2 contains a fix for this issue.

docs.title: multiScan200
docs.text:
multiScan200 3D LiDAR sensor.

The multiScan200 is a compact 3D LiDAR sensor family with high detection reliability in harsh environments. The first variant is the multiScan270. Use the Product ID (PID) to find the exact product variant on sick.com: enter the part number (P/N) and optional serial number (S/N), for example 1134610/25250710. A complete pid.sick.com URL is also accepted.

Product ID pid.sick.com/ Open product

Supported inputs, onboard processing functions, and outputs for the multiScan200.

Input Processing Output CoLa A/B Angle-range focus filtering CoLa A/B telegrams Digital inputs Blooming filtering Compact over TCP Gigabit Ethernet Compact 3D scanning Contamination status HTTPS Contamination indication Device status NTP Device discovery Diagnostic and error data PTP Echo filtering Digital outputs REST API Field evaluation Field-evaluation states SOPASair Interval filtering Native ROS 2 topics Particle filtering REST JSON responses Sensitivity modes Synchronized timestamps Time synchronization

docs.title: CoLa Telegram Listing
docs.text: This reference lists the CoLa telegrams supported by the multiScan200. Use the command details to build or troubleshoot PLC and other low-level integrations without guessing the telegram structure.

docs.title: Log In [sMN SetAccessMode]
docs.text:
A log in to the device is necessary to change parameters. In most cases, the user level 'Authorized client' is needed. On delivery, only the Service user level is enabled; until a Service user enables Maintenance or Authorized client, the device answers a log in with these levels with sAN SetAccessMode 0 (see User Levels). Changed parameters will be reset to the previous state via a reboot unless they are saved. To save parameter changes the command "sMN mEEwriteall" must be sent before log out.

Telegram structure: sMN SetAccessMode

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Method String 3 sMN 73 4D 4E Command User level String 13 SetAccessMode 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 User level Select user level Int_8 1 Maintenance:Authorized client:Service: 234 020304 Password Hash value for the selected user level Uint_32 4 Maintenance:Authorized client:Service: B21ACE26F472474481BE23AA B2 1A CE 26F4 72 47 4481 BE 23 AA

docs.title: Change Password [sMN SetPassword]
docs.text:
Change the log in password of a user level. If you are logged in with a higher user level, you can also set the password of lower user levels.

The password is sent as a hash value. To calculate it, log in to SOPASair as Service and open Diagnosis > Cybersecurity > Hash calculator. For example, the hash value of the password testtest is 1920E4C9.

docs.title: Set Scan Configuration [sMN mCLsetscancfglist]
docs.text:
Select the scan configuration (field of view, scanning frequency, and angular resolution) by its number. Scan configurations 10 to 12 use interlace mode: they achieve a higher angular resolution by combining scans that are shifted to each other. The supported scan configurations are listed in the parameter table below. Read the active scan configuration with sRN PerformanceProfileNumber. To set it, use sWN PerformanceProfileNumber.

In CoLa A, a number without a sign is hexadecimal: send scan configuration 10 as +10 or A, not as 10.

docs.text:

docs.title: Set Particle Filter [sWN particleFilter]
docs.text:
Configure the particle filter. A point is a particle if fewer than the minimum number of neighbors in its 8-connected neighborhood, over all echoes, are within the distance threshold. See Filter Details.

Required user level: Authorized client.

Telegram structure: sWN particleFilter

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Write request String 3 sWN 73 57 4E Variable name Particle filter String 14 particleFilter 70 61 72 74 69 63 6C 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 enable If true a detected particle is filtered out (aka distance set to zero) and subsequent echoes are moved up. Otherwise, the point is flagged in the properties channel. Bool_1 1 False:True: 01 0001 minNumberOfNeighbors If a measurement has less points in its 8-connected neighborhood over all echoes within the distance threshold, this measurement is considered as particle. Uint_16 2 Max: 8 +1 00 01 distanceThreshold Distance threshold value. For a given measurement all points in the 8-connected neighborhood over all three echoes are with a distance less than the distanceThreshold are counted. If the result is below the minNumberOfNeighbors, this measurement is considered as particle Uint_16 2 Max: 2000 +500 01 F4

docs.title: Set Angle Range Focus Filter [sWN angleRangeFocusFilter]
docs.text:
Restricts streaming data output to a specified 3D field of view. The theta parameters define the azimuth range and the phi parameters define the elevation range. Beams outside these ranges are not transmitted. Within the selected range, subsampling can be applied to reduce data bandwidth. Additionally, a focus region can be defined where full resolution is preserved (no subsampling). This filter only affects raw data streaming and has no effect on object detection.

Required user level: Authorized client.

Telegram structure: sWN angleRangeFocusFilter

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Write request String 3 sWN 73 57 4E Variable name Restricts streaming data output to a specified 3D field of view. The theta parameters define the azimuth range and the phi parameters define the elevation range. Beams outside these ranges are not transmitted. Within the selected range, subsampling can be applied to reduce data bandwidth. Additionally, a focus region can be defined where full resolution is preserved (no subsampling). This filter only affects raw data streaming and has no effect on object detection. String 21 angleRangeFocusFilter 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 6F 63 75 73 46 69 6C 74 65 72 enable Enables/Disables the filter. Bool_1 1 False:True: 01 0001 thetaStart Lower boundary of the azimuth range. Columns outside this range are not transmitted. Int_32 4 -900000 FF F2 44 60 thetaStop Upper boundary of the azimuth range. Columns outside this range are not transmitted. Int_32 4 +900000 00 0D BB A0 phiStart Lower boundary of the elevation range. Layers outside this range are not transmitted. Int_32 4 -250000 FF FC 2F 70 phiStop Upper boundary of the elevation range. Layers outside this range are not transmitted. Int_32 4 +250000 00 03 D0 90 thetaIndexIncrement The 'thetaIndexIncrement' is used to sub-sample the slots within the selected theta angle range. With a 'thetaIndexIncrement' of n only every n'th slot from the selected angle range is serialized, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. Uint_16 2 +1 00 01 phiIndexIncrement The 'phiIndexIncrement' is used to sub-sample the layers within the selected phi angle range. With a 'phiIndex-Increment' of n only every n'th layer from the selected angle range is serialized, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. Uint_16 2 +1 00 01 enable Enables/Disables the focus region. In this region, the sub-sampling is not applied. Bool_1 1 False:True: 01 0001 direction Focus direction: selects whether the focus region spans the vertical or horizontal axis. Enum_8 1 0 00 thetaStart Lower boundary of the azimuth focus range Int_32 4 -450000 FF F9 22 30 thetaStop Upper boundary of the azimuth focus range Int_32 4 +450000 00 06 DD D0 phiStart Lower boundary of the elevation focus range Int_32 4 -100000 FF FE 79 60 phiStop Upper boundary of the elevation focus range Int_32 4 +100000 00 01 86 A0

docs.text:
The telegram is intended to read the current configuration state of the field evaluation. Depending on the device, computational limits can be reached. docs.title: Read Field Evaluation Result [sRN FieldEvaluationResult]
docs.text:
This telegram returns the status information of all evaluations. Possible status codes:

  • Not configured - This evaluation has not been configured.
  • Inactive - This evaluation has been configured but is currently not evaluated.
  • Free - The field is not infringed.
  • Infringed - The field is infringed.
  • Detecting infringed - An infringement has been detected in the field but the response time has not been reached yet.
  • Detecting free - The field is no longer infringed but the time for the free state has not been reached yet.

docs.title: Error Codes [sFA]
docs.text:
If the device cannot execute a telegram, it answers with sFA and an error code, for example sFA 3 (CoLa A) or 73 46 41 00 03 (CoLa B payload) for an unknown variable name.

Error code Description Dec. Hex. Sopas_Ok No error 0 0 Sopas_Error_METHODIN_ACCESSDENIED Wrong userlevel, access to method not allowed 1 1 Sopas_Error_METHODIN_UNKNOWNINDEX Trying to access a method with an unknown Sopas index 2 2 Sopas_Error_VARIABLE_UNKNOWNINDEX Trying to access a variable with an unknown Sopas index 3 3 Sopas_Error_LOCALCONDITIONFAILED Local condition violated, e.g. giving a value that exceeds the minimum or maximum allowed value for this variable 4 4 Sopas_Error_INVALID_DATA Invalid data given for variable, this errorcode is deprecated (is not used anymore). 5 5 Sopas_Error_UNKNOWN_ERROR An error with unknown reason occurred, this errorcode is deprecated. 6 6 Sopas_Error_BUFFER_OVERFLOW The communication buffer was too small for the amount of data that should be serialised. 7 7 Sopas_Error_BUFFER_UNDERFLOW More data was expected, the allocated buffer could not be filled. 8 8 Sopas_Error_ERROR_UNKNOWN_TYPE The variable that shall be serialised has an unknown type. This can only happen when there are variables in the firmware of the device that do not exist in the released description of the device. This should never happen. 9 9 Sopas_Error_VARIABLE_WRITE_ACCESSDENIED It is not allowed to write values to this variable. Probably the variable is defined as read-only. 10 A Sopas_Error_UNKNOWN_CMD_FOR_NAMESERVER When using names instead of indices, a command was issued that the nameserver does not understand. 11 B Sopas_Error_UNKNOWN_COLA_COMMAND The CoLa protocol specification does not define the given command, command is unknown. 12 C Sopas_Error_METHODIN_SERVER_BUSY It is not possible to issue more than one command at a time to an SRT device. 13 D Sopas_Error_FLEX_OUTOF_BOUNDS An array was accessed over its maximum length. 14 E Sopas_Error_EVENTREG_UNKNOWNINDEX The event you wanted to register for does not exist, the index is unknown. 15 F Sopas_Error_COLA_A_VALUE_OVERFLOW The value does not fit into the value field, it is too large. 16 10 Sopas_Error_COLA_A_INVALIDCHARACTER Character is unknown, probably not alphanumeric. 17 11 Sopas_Error_OSAI_NO_MESSAGE Only when using SRTOS in the firmware and distributed variables this error can occur. It is an indication that no operating system message could be created. This happens when trying to GET a variable. 18 12 Sopas_Error_OSAI_NO_ANSWER_MESSAGE This is the same as Sopas_Error_OSAI_NO_MESSAGE with the difference that it is thrown when trying to PUT a variable. 19 13 Sopas_Error_INTERNAL Internal error in the firmware, probably a pointer to a parameter was null. 20 14 Sopas_Error_HubAddressCorrupted The Sopas Hubaddress is either too short or too long. 21 15 Sopas_Error_HubAddressDecoding The Sopas Hubaddress is invalid, it can not be decoded (Syntax). 22 16 Sopas_Error_HubAddressAddressExceeded Too many hubs in the address 23 17 Sopas_Error_HubAddressBlankExpected When parsing a HubAddress an expected blank was not found. The HubAddress is not valid. 24 18 - An asynchronous method call was made although the device was built with “AsyncMethodsSuppressed”. This is an internal error that should never happen in a released device. 25 19 - Device was built with „ComplexArraysSuppressed“ because the compiler does not allow recursions. But now a complex array was found. This is an internal error that should never happen in a released device. 26 1A

docs.title: Contamination Indication
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

Contamination indication monitors the sensor's optics cover for dirt that could reduce measurement quality. It evaluates contamination by sector so maintenance can target the affected area and be scheduled before the optics become too dirty. picoScan100 evaluates seven sectors; its SOPASair sector display shows where contamination is accumulating, with overall states of Clean, Minor, Heavy, and Blocked.

Configure the sensitivity, response time, warning threshold, and active sectors for the installation. The device can expose the result through its GUI and REST API; depending on configuration, it can also be monitored through CoLa or mapped to digital outputs. The warning and error behavior, and whether blocked sectors count as errors, are configurable. Use the indication as a maintenance signal and inspect and clean the optics according to the product documentation.

All contamination settings and results are available through the REST API. The endpoints are listed under Contamination Indication in the LRS4000 REST API, multiScan100 REST API, multiScan200 REST API, and picoScan100 REST API references.

Writes require the Authorized Client user level and challenge-response authentication. Persist configuration changes with WriteEeprom; otherwise, they may be lost after a power cycle.

picoScan100 CoLa clients can read configuration and sector data and subscribe to event-driven contamination updates. See the picoScan100 CoLa Telegram Listing. For the interface walkthrough, see Contamination Indication in SOPASair.

docs.title: Field Evaluation
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 multiScan200 picoScan100

The sensor evaluates detection zones on the device. Field evaluation checks whether scan points enter a configured polygon and reports a FREE or INFRINGED result. The result can drive a digital output and can be read through REST or CoLa where the product exposes those interfaces.

picoScan100: How to draw fields and detect objects?

docs.title: Configure an Evaluation
docs.text:
Create evaluation groups in SOPASair, or restore them from a configuration file. The REST API and CoLa can then change existing evaluations or, on the picoScan100, build complete evaluations from scratch (see Configure Over The API). Call WriteEeprom after changes to store them permanently.

Configure an Evaluation: REST resource, purpose, and devices.

REST resource Purpose Devices SetFieldEvaluationContour Writes the polygon of an evaluation LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan100 GetFieldEvaluationContour Reads the polygon of an evaluation LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan100 SetFieldEvaluationConfiguration / GetFieldEvaluationConfiguration Writes or reads evaluation parameters multiScan200 EvaluationGroupType Selects field evaluation or perpendicular-distance mode LRS4000, picoScan100 PortConfiguration Configures I/O ports, including outputs used by evaluations LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, picoScan100

docs.title: Activate and Monitor a Group
docs.text:
A group can be active continuously (ALWAYS), controlled by inputs (INPUTS), or controlled by a telegram (TELEGRAM). ActivateEvaluationGroup only affects groups configured with TELEGRAM; it cannot switch an ALWAYS group.

Activate and Monitor a Group: REST resource and purpose.

REST resource Purpose ActivateEvaluationGroup Activates or deactivates a TELEGRAM-controlled group FieldEvaluationGroupState Group state: not configured, active, or inactive FieldEvaluationResult Current result: FREE, INFRINGED, or a transitional state; also available as a WebSocket event

A typical application creates the groups once, persists the configuration, and at runtime reads the group state and result, updates contours when necessary, and switches telegram-controlled groups.

For full payloads, see the LRS4000, multiScan100, multiScan200, and picoScan100 REST API references and the device-specific CoLa telegram listings.

docs.title: Configure over the API
docs.text:
Compatible with: picoScan100

On the picoScan100, REST and CoLa expose every variable needed to create, change, and delete a field evaluation without SOPASair. The following workflow applies to picoScan150 with firmware V2.3.3. Some of these variables, such as Eval001–Eval048 and EvaluationGroupMapping, are not listed in the published OpenAPI file, but can be read and written as REST variables (GET / POST /api/<Variable>).

Configure over the API: variable or method and purpose.

Variable or method Purpose Eval001–Eval048 Detection parameters of one evaluation slot: mode, minimum object size, timing, and the referenced volume (VolumeList) SetFieldEvaluationContour / GetFieldEvaluationContour Writes or reads the polygon of an evaluation EvaluationGroupMapping Groups evaluations and sets the activation type of each group PortConfiguration Assigns an evaluation result to a digital output ActivateEvaluationGroup Switches a TELEGRAM group on or off; needs no login FieldEvaluationGroupState / FieldEvaluationResult Read-only group state and evaluation result WriteEeprom (REST) / mEEwriteall (CoLa) Stores the configuration permanently

To create an evaluation, log in as Authorized client or Service and write the variables in this order:

  1. Write EvalNNN with the detection mode, the minimum object size, and VolumeList = [NNN].
  2. Write the polygon with SetFieldEvaluationContour. It returns error 1 (invalid evaluation) if VolumeList of the slot is empty, so write the slot first.
  3. Write EvaluationGroupMapping. The whole array is replaced on every write: read the current mapping first and include every group you want to keep.
  4. Optional: write PortConfiguration to switch a digital output when the evaluation is infringed. Outputs refer to evaluations (sources EG01–EG48), not to groups, and the whole port array must be written.
  5. Call WriteEeprom. The device re-initializes; wait about 1 s before reading the state.
  6. For a TELEGRAM group, switch it on with ActivateEvaluationGroup.

To delete an evaluation, remove its group from EvaluationGroupMapping, clear VolumeList and the name of the slot, and call WriteEeprom. The group state returns to not configured.

The coordinates are in millimeters in the sensor coordinate system: x points forward (depth) and y to the side.

Detection modes (EvaluationParamsCommon.Mode of the evaluation slot):

Configure over the API: value, mode, and the field is infringed when.

Value Mode The field is infringed when 0 Blanking An object at least as large as the minimum object size is inside the field. This is the most common mode. 1 Reflector only A highly reflective object such as a retroreflector is inside the field. 2 Contour The scan deviates from the taught-in contour by more than the tolerance. Requires a valid teach-in.

Activation types (Activation.Type of a group):

Configure over the API: value, type, and behavior.

Value Type Behavior 0 Deactivated The group is never evaluated. 1 Always The group is active as soon as it is stored. ActivateEvaluationGroup returns false for it and cannot switch it off. 2 Inputs Digital inputs activate the group. 3 Telegram The group starts in the state set by InitialActivationStateTelegram and is switched with ActivateEvaluationGroup.

FieldEvaluationGroupState returns one value per group: 0 not configured, 1 active, 2 inactive. FieldEvaluationResult returns one state per evaluation: 0 not configured, 1 inactive, 2 free, 3 detecting infringed, 4 infringed, 5 detecting free.

For complete REST and CoLa payloads of every step, see the knowledge base article picoScan150: Field Evaluation and Perpendicular Distance API Possibilities.

docs.title: Editing Field Polygons
docs.text: Field polygons can be changed through the web GUI, configuration import, REST, CoLa, or the SDK. Select the method that fits whether the change is an interactive adjustment, a repeatable deployment, or an application-driven update.

docs.title: Web GUI Configuration
docs.text:
Open the Object Detection application in SOPASair to create and edit polygon points directly. This is the quickest method for commissioning and manual adjustments. The field editor also supports teach-in.

Field evaluation teach-in tile in SOPASair.

For bulk coordinate changes, open the Field settings dialog and select JSON in its footer toolbar. The editor switches from the coordinate table to a JSON text field. Paste the prepared polygon to replace all points at once:

{
  "points": [
    { "x": -5, "y": 531 },
    { "x": 837, "y": 565 },
    { "x": 907, "y": -637 },
    { "x": 12, "y": -590 }
  ]
}

docs.title: Configuration File Import
docs.text: Use the top-right SOPASair menu to download the complete configuration from a commissioned sensor. It includes field geometries and can be imported into another compatible device, making it suitable for repeatable commissioning and replacement devices. Keep a versioned, validated backup for each deployed configuration.

docs.title: Programmatic Updates
docs.text:
The REST API exposes SetFieldEvaluationContour to update a polygon. The evaluation must already exist. Use GetFieldEvaluationContour to confirm the stored geometry and persist the change with WriteEeprom. See Configure An Evaluation and the REST client example.

CoLa provides the same SetFieldEvaluationContour function through its telegram interface. Use it when the integration already uses CoLa, such as a PLC or legacy client; see CoLa.

The sick_perception_sdk uses the REST interface and provides an application-level option for changing contours. See the object-detection example.

docs.title: Distance-Dependent
docs.text:
The Distance-dependent parameter determines whether two detected objects are evaluated separately or merged into one object based on their axial separation. It works with the configured Blanking width to avoid triggering a field evaluation when separate small objects would otherwise appear as one large object.

picoScan100: 2D Object Detection Parameter Distance-dependent.

The video uses two objects: a foreground object approximately 60 mm wide, a background object approximately 250 mm wide, and about 450 mm of axial separation. The standard blanking width is 300 mm.

Example: configuration, result, and explanation.

Configuration Result Explanation Distance-dependent off Field infringed Both objects merge into one contiguous object wider than 300 mm. Distance-dependent on; threshold 300 mm Field not infringed The objects are at least 300 mm apart and are evaluated separately; neither is wider than 300 mm. Distance-dependent on; threshold 500 mm Field infringed The objects are less than 500 mm apart, so they merge and exceed the blanking width.

Set the separation threshold to the distance at which nearby objects should be merged for your application. See Configure An Evaluation for the evaluation and polygon.

docs.title: Teach In
docs.text: Teach-in captures the current environment and uses the measured contour as a field for object detection. Use it during commissioning when the surrounding geometry should define the detection field instead of drawing a polygon manually.

docs.title: Web GUI Teach In
docs.text:
Open the Object Detection application in SOPASair and select Teach-in in the field configuration. Set the distances in front of and behind the object, choose the minimum teach-in time, and click Start. Stop the teach-in when the environment has been captured, then save the field evaluation configuration.

Teach-in configuration in SOPASair.

The configured distances take effect during the next teach-in. Keep the intended environment stable while the contour is captured.

Teach-in uses the same evaluation group and output mechanism as a manually configured field. After the contour has been captured, monitor the evaluation result through the configured output, REST, CoLa, or WebSocket events.

docs.title: Teach in over the API
docs.text:
A teach-in evaluation is an evaluation slot with mode 2 (contour). The polygon written with SetFieldEvaluationContour is not the detection field: it is the region of interest in which teach-in learns the reference contour. GetFieldEvaluationContour therefore returns this region, not the learned contour.

Teach-in is global; it is not bound to an evaluation slot. Set the parameters, then start and stop the teach-in:

Teach in over the API: variable or method and purpose.

Variable or method Purpose TeachInToleranceFront / TeachInToleranceBack Tolerance in front of and behind the taught contour, in mm (default 250) TeachInMinimumTimeMs Minimum teach-in time, 100 to 60000 ms (default 250) TeachInActivationInput Digital input that starts the teach-in; 0 = software only StartTeachIn / StopTeachIn Starts and stops the teach-in TeachInActive 1 while the teach-in runs TeachInContourValid 1 after a teach-in produced a valid contour

Keep the scene stable for at least the minimum teach-in time, stop the teach-in, check TeachInContourValid, and call WriteEeprom. To change the field later, repeat the teach-in, for example with a larger tolerance; the region of interest stays the same.

docs.title: Ground Filter (multiScan100)
docs.text:
The ground filter uses upper and lower ground thresholds to reduce false field-evaluation triggers caused by the ground. When configured correctly, it retains small objects such as forklift tines and can be used indoors and outdoors. The filter also affects perpendicular-distance evaluations. See Ground Filter for availability and API settings.

multiScan1xx: Ground-filter behavior in a field application.

docs.title: Perpendicular Distance Measurement
docs.text:
Compatible with: LRS4000 multiScan100 picoScan100

Perpendicular distance evaluation measures object distances relative to a reference line in the scan plane. Define a field and reference line in the application; the sensor evaluates the points in that field and reports the minimum and maximum perpendicular distances and the positions of the corresponding measuring points.

multiScan1xx: Perpendicular distance application demonstration.

docs.title: Configure a Measurement
docs.text:
1. Open Application > Perpendicular distance measurement in SOPASair and add an evaluation group.
  2. Draw the zone in which objects should be measured.
  3. Set Max. blanking size and Detection time under Object detection to balance measurement stability and response time for the target.
  4. Save the configuration to the device.
  5. Check the live minimum and maximum distances and their measuring-point coordinates in the result list.

The evaluation runs on the sensor, so the host receives measurement results without having to detect objects from the raw scan itself. See the SOPASair configuration walkthrough for the interface details.

docs.title: Read Results
docs.text:
The REST endpoint GET /api/perpendicularDistanceResult returns a timestamp and an evaluations array. Each result contains an evaluation ID, minimum and maximum distance, and the 3D position of each corresponding measuring point. The evaluations array is empty when no object is measured. The result is read-only; see the picoScan100 REST API reference.

CoLa clients can poll sRN perpendicularDistanceResult for the current measurement or subscribe with sEN perpendicularDistanceResult for event updates. The telegram reports the shortest and furthest measuring point in the range relative to the reference plane. See the picoScan100 CoLa Telegram Listing.

docs.title: Configure over the API (picoScan100)
docs.text:
REST and CoLa expose every variable needed to create, change, and delete a perpendicular distance evaluation without SOPASair. The following workflow applies to picoScan150 with firmware V2.3.3. Some of these variables are not listed in the published OpenAPI file, but can be read and written as REST variables (GET / POST /api/<Variable>).

A perpendicular distance evaluation has two parts, as in SOPASair:

Configure over the API (picoScan100): part, variables, and content.

Part Variables Content Object detection EvalNNN, VolumeNNN Detection parameters (blanking mode, minimum object size, detection time) and the field in which objects are measured Reference line perpDistNNN Normal vector of the line in the scan plane and its signed distance from the sensor, in mm

To create an evaluation, log in as Authorized client or Service and write the variables in this order, using the same slot number NNN throughout:

  1. Set the slot to perpendicular distance: write EvaluationGroupType with all 48 values and 1 at the slot position (0 = field evaluation).
  2. Write EvalNNN with VolumeList = [NNN].
  3. Write the field polygon directly to VolumeNNN. Do not use SetFieldEvaluationContour here: it returns success for perpendicular distance slots but is not reliable for them.
  4. Write the reference line to perpDistNNN. The normal vector sets the orientation, for example (1, 0, 0) for a line across the forward direction, and the distance sets its position. Because the picoScan100 is a 2D sensor, the z component is always 0. The no-data mode sets the output when no object is measured: 0 zero, 1 hold the last value, or 2 a user-defined substitution distance.
  5. Add the group to EvaluationGroupMapping with EvalIds = [NNN]. The whole array is replaced on every write, so include every group you want to keep.
  6. Call WriteEeprom and wait about 1 s before reading the result.

Keep in mind:

  • Perpendicular distance groups need their own slots; they cannot share a slot with a field evaluation group.
  • If the field is missing (empty VolumeList or empty VolumeNNN) or the group references no evaluation, the device reports a recoverable error (DeviceStatus = 7 instead of 3) and the result stays empty.
  • Perpendicular distance results are not assigned to digital outputs; read them from perpendicularDistanceResult.
  • Group activation (ALWAYS, INPUTS, TELEGRAM) and ActivateEvaluationGroup work as for field evaluation.

To delete the evaluation, remove the group from EvaluationGroupMapping, clear EvalNNN, VolumeNNN, and perpDistNNN, set the slot in EvaluationGroupType back to 0, and call WriteEeprom.

For complete REST and CoLa payloads of every step, see the knowledge base article picoScan150: Field Evaluation and Perpendicular Distance API Possibilities.

For output and evaluation-group concepts shared with field evaluation, see Field Evaluation.

docs.title: picoScan100
docs.text:
picoScan100 2D LiDAR sensor.

The picoScan100 is a compact 2D LiDAR sensor with one scan plane and a 276° scan range. It comes in two variants: the picoScan120 and the picoScan150. Use the Product ID (PID) to find the exact product variant on sick.com: enter the part number (P/N) and optional serial number (S/N), for example 1134610/25250710. A complete pid.sick.com URL is also accepted.

docs.title: Log In [sMN SetAccessMode]
docs.text:
A log in to the device is necessary to change parameters. In most cases, the user level 'Authorized client' is needed. Changed parameters will be reset to the previous state via a reboot unless they are saved. To save parameter changes the command "sMN mEEwriteall" must be sent before log out.

Telegram structure: sMN SetAccessMode

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Method String 3 sMN 73 4D 4E Command User level String 13 SetAccessMode 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 User level Select user level Int_8 1 Maintenance:Authorized client:Service: 234 020304 Password Hash value for the selected user level Uint_32 4 Maintenance:Authorized client:Service: B21ACE26F472474481BE23AA B2 1A CE 26F4 72 47 4481 BE 23 AA

Example: sMN SetAccessMode - Log in as “Authorized client” with password “F4724744”

Protocol Example CoLa A <STX>sMN{SPC}SetAccessMode{SPC}3{SPC}F4724744<ETX> CoLa A <STX>sMN SetAccessMode 3 F4724744<ETX> CoLa A sMN SetAccessMode 3 F4724744 CoLa A 02 73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 30 33 20 46 34 37 32 34 37 34 34 03 CoLa B 02 02 02 02 00 00 00 17 73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 03 F4 72 47 44 B3 CoLa B 73 4D 4E 20 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 20 03 F4 72 47 44

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Answer String 3 sAN 73 41 4E Command User level String 13 SetAccessMode 53 65 74 41 63 63 65 73 73 4D 6F 64 65 Change user level Changed level Bool_1 1 Error:Success: 01 0001

docs.title: Read for Frequency and Angular Resolution [sRN LMPscancfg]
docs.text:
Read the scanning frequency, angular resolution and aperture angle of the device. Values show the information of the values before any filters are applied. Therefore aperture angle is always showing the maximum, scanning frequency and angular resolution may also be static depending on device family.

Telegram structure: sRN LMPscancfg

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Read String 3 sRN 73 52 4E Command Info of scan frequency and angular resolution String 10 LMPscancfg 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67

Example: sRN LMPscancfg

Protocol Example CoLa A <STX>sRN{SPC}LMPscancfg<ETX> CoLa A <STX>sRN LMPscancfg<ETX> CoLa A sRN LMPscancfg CoLa A 02 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 03 CoLa B 02 02 02 02 00 00 00 0E 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67 63 CoLa B 73 52 4E 20 4C 4D 50 73 63 61 6E 63 66 67

docs.title: Autostart Measurement [sWN LMPautostartmeas]
docs.text:
This parameter defines whether the scanner will start to rotate directly and measure when powering up or remain in idle mode. The changed setting (saved with the command sMN mEEWriteall, ) will be then be active with the next power-up cycle.

In case autostart is deactivated, the sensor will remain in idle mode with the laser switched off and a motor speed depending on the Dynamic Sensing Profile .

Telegram structure: sWN LMPautostartmeas

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Write String 3 sWN 73 57 4E Command Autostart measurement String 16 LMPautostartmeas 4C 4D 50 61 75 74 6F 73 74 61 72 74 6D 65 61 73 Status code Activate / Deactivate Autostart Bool_1 1 Autostart off:Autostart on: 01 0001

docs.title: Read Checksum [sRN LFTchecksum]
docs.text:
This command includes the MD5 checksum of multiple software parts to verify their integrity. The checksums help to ensure files have not been corrupted or altered. They are also important for cybersecurity because they detect unauthorized modifications.

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Read String 3 sRN 73 52 4E Command MD5 checksum String 11 LFTchecksum 4C 46 54 63 68 65 63 6B 73 75 6D

docs.title: Change Password [sMN SetPassword]
docs.text:
Changing the log in password for a specific user level.

If logged in with a higher user level you may set the password for lower user levels as well.

docs.title: Send Data Permanently [sEN LMDscandata]
docs.text:
Start/ stop continuous retrievement of measurement data from device. Data will be transmitted as configured as soon as measurement data is generated by the device. No data is generated when there is an active log in, the laser is shut off (e.g. in Standby mode), the motor is stopped or in case of certain error modes (e.g. Device not ready).

Data is transmitted only via LMDscandata when LMDscandata is selected as data output format.

During the boot-up phase of the device, there will be no data telegram or answer from the device.

Telegram structure: sEN LMDscandata

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Event String 3 sEN 73 45 4E Command Data telegram String 11 LMDscandata 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 Measurement Start/stop Enum_8 1 Stop:Start: 01 0001

Example: sEN LMDscandata

Protocol Example CoLa A <STX>sEN{SPC}LMDscandata{SPC}1<ETX> CoLa A <STX>sEN LMDscandata 1<ETX> CoLa A sEN LMDscandata 1 CoLa A 02 73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 31 03 CoLa B 02 02 02 02 00 00 00 11 73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 01 33 CoLa B 73 45 4E 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 01

Telegram structure: sEA LMDscandata

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Answer String 3 sEA 73 45 41 Command Data telegram String 11 LMDscandata 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 Measurement Start/stop Enum_8 1 Stop:Start: 01 0001

Example: Confirmation of sEA LMDscandata

Protocol Example CoLa A <STX>sEA{SPC}LMDscandata{SPC}1<ETX> CoLa A 02 73 45 41 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 31 03 CoLa B 02 02 02 02 00 00 00 11 73 45 41 20 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 20 01 3C

The answer to the telegram will be followed by the scandata:

Telegram structure: Datastream of sRA LMDscandata/sSN LMDscandata

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Read String 3 Answer to sRN LMDscandata:Answer to sEN LMDscandata: sRAsSN 73 52 4173 53 4E Command Data telegram String 11 LMDscandata 4C 4D 44 73 63 61 6E 64 61 74 61 Version number For detecting format changes by the version. Uint_16 2 1h … FFFFh 00 01 … FF FF Device Device number Defined with SOPAS Uint_16 2 0h … FFFFh 00 00 … FF FF Serial number Production period (year, calendar week, number): YYWWxxxx Uint_32 4 0h … FFFFFFFFh 00 00 00 00 … FF FF FF FF Device status (See values column) Uint_8 2 x 1 Ok:Error: 0 01 0 00 0001 00 Status info Telegram counter Number of measurement telegrams finished in the scanner and given to the interface. Does not count how many telegrams were really given out; is relevant if not all scans are delivered from the scan core. Uint_16 2 0h … FFFFh 00 00 … FF FF Scan counter Number of scans which were created in the device; counts how many scans were really done. Uint_16 2 0h … FFFFh 00 00 … FF FF Time since start up in µs In the output telegram this is the time at the zero index before the measurement itself starts. Time base is the boot-up time in µs since power up, max. 71 min then starting from 0 again. Time base is the boot-up time in µs since power up, max. 71 min then starting from 0 again. Uint_32 4 0h … FFFFFFFFh 00 00 00 00 … FF FF FF FF Status of digital inputs Low byte represents input 1. Uint_8 2 x 1 All outputs low:All outputs high: 0 03 F 00 0003 0F Reserved - Uint_16 2 Always: 0 00 00 00 00 Frequencies Scan frequency [1/100 Hz] Uint_32 4 15 Hz ... 50 Hz:(depends on Dynamic Sensing Profile ) 5DCh ... 1388h 05 DC ... 13 88 Reserved - Uint_32 4 Always: 0 00 00 00 00 Encoder Amount of encoder If 0, then next two telegram parts are missing. FFh 00 ... FF Reserved Reserved - Enum_16 2 Always: 0 00 00 Reserved Reserved - Enum_16 2 Always: 0 00 00 Reserved Reserved - Enum_16 2 Always: 0 00 00 Reserved Reserved - Enum_16 2 Always: 0 00 00 Reserved Reserved - Uint_16 2 Always: 0 00 00

LMDscandata - reserved values

Valid distance measurement values are values starting from 16d upwards; everything below has the following meaning:

DIST RSSI Description 0d 0d Invalid measurement value; caused by very low remission (extremely dark object), object distance not within measurement range (too close or too far away) or selected filter settings at device 1d - 15d 0d Reserved, currently not in use ≥16d >0h Valid measurement values ≥16d 254d Reflector detected ≥16d 255d Reserved

Higher measurement values will be given out with a zero, that means no measurement value detected.

docs.title: Set Time Stamp [sMN LSPsetdatetime]
docs.text:
The data format in the telegram is: +2009{SPC}+7{SPC}+22{SPC}+12{SPC}+0{SPC}+0{SPC}+0.The numbers represent year, month, day, hour, minute, second, microsecond.

If plus is used up-front the data it is interpreted as an integer decimal number, without the plus it's the scanner reads the data as hex format.

The answer is always in ASCII format.

Does only work if NTP- respectively PTP-Client is not active.

There is no real time clock inside the device. When the scanner is switched off and after a reboot, the time has to be set again. Therefore, it is recommended to use a NTP or a PTP setting.

Telegram structure: sMN LSPsetdatetime

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Method String 3 sMN 73 4D 4E Command Set time stamp String 14 LSPsetdatetime 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 Year Uint_16 2 +1970d … +2099d (07B2h … 0833h) 07 B2 … 08 33 Month Uint_8 1 +1d … +12d(01h … 0Ch) 01 … 0C Day Uint_8 1 +1d … +31d(01h … 1Fh) 00 … 1F Hour Uint_8 1 +0d … +23d(00h … 17h) 00 … 17 Minute Uint_8 1 +0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh) 00 … 3B Second Uint_8 1 +0d … +59d(00h … 3Bh) 00 … 3B Microsecond Uint_32 4 +0d … +999999d(00000000h … 000F423Fh) 00 00 00 00 … 00 0F 42 3F

Example 1: sMN LSPsetdatetime Date: 17.02.2009; Time: 16:34

Protocol Example CoLa A <STX>sMN{SPC}LSPsetdatetime{SPC}7D9{SPC}2{SPC}11{SPC}10{SPC}22{SPC}0{SPC}0<ETX> CoLa A <STX>sMN LSPsetdatetime 7D9 2 11 10 22 0 0<ETX> CoLa A sMN LSPsetdatetime 7D9 2 11 10 22 0 0 CoLa A 02 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 37 44 39 20 32 20 31 31 20 31 30 20 32 32 20 30 20 30 03 CoLa B 02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1E 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 D9 02 11 10 22 00 00 00 00 00 A3 CoLa B 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 D9 02 11 10 22 00 00 00 00 00

Example 2: sMN LSPsetdatetime Date: 26.01.2010; Time: 10:35

Protocol Example CoLa A <STX>sMN{SPC}LSPsetdatetime{SPC}+2010{SPC}+01{SPC}+26{SPC}+10{SPC}+35{SPC}0{SPC}0<ETX> CoLa A <STX>sMN LSPsetdatetime +2010 +01 +26 +10 +35 0 0<ETX> CoLa A sMN LSPsetdatetime +2010 +01 +26 +10 +35 0 0 CoLa A 02 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 2B 32 30 31 30 20 2B 30 31 20 2B 32 36 20 2B 31 30 20 2B 33 35 20 2B 30 30 20 2B 30 30 30 30 03 CoLa B 02 02 02 02 00 00 00 1E 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 DA 01 1A 0A 23 00 00 00 00 00 B3 CoLa B 73 4D 4E 20 4C 53 50 73 65 74 64 61 74 65 74 69 6D 65 20 07 DA 01 1A 0A 23 00 00 00 00 00

docs.title: Set Angle Range Filter [sWN LFPangleRangeFilter]
docs.text:
The angle range filter set up the horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) start- and stop angle in rad.

BeamIncrement = the 'beamIncrement' which is used to subsample the beams within the selected angle range. With a 'beamIncrement' of n only every nth beam from the selected angle range is copied to the output scan, i.e. the angle resolution is reduced by factor n. If the beamIncrement is zero it is set to one.

Telegram structure: sWN LFPangleRangeFilter

Telegram part Description Variable Length Additional details Values CoLa A (ASCII) Values CoLa B (Binary) Command type Write String 3 sWN 73 57 4E Command filter set up the horizontal (theta) and vertical (phi) start- and stop angle in rad String 19 LFPangleRangeFilter 4C 46 50 61 6E 67 6C 65 52 61 6E 67 65 46 69 6C 74 65 72 Variable Data 1 Enables/Disables the filter Bool_1 1 Off:On: +0d+1d 0001 Variable Data 2 ThetaStart Real 4 No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) -1,800,000d ... +1,800,000d (FFE488C0 ... 001B7740h) FF E4 88 C0 … 00 1B 77 40 Variable Data 3 ThetaStop Real 4 No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) -1,800,000d ... +1,800,000d (FFE488C0 ... 001B7740h) FF E4 88 C0 … 00 1B 77 40 Variable Data 4 PhiStart Real 4 No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) -900,000d ... +900,000d (FFF24460 ... 000DBBA0h) FF F2 44 60 … 00 0D BB A0 Variable Data 5 PhiStop Real 4 No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) -900,000d ... +900,000d (FFF24460 ... 000DBBA0h) FF F2 44 60 … 00 0D BB A0 Variable Data 6 BeamIncrement UInt_16 2 No impact on sensor setting but needs to be filled (see example) 1d…+20d 00 01 … 00 14

Explanation: Enable the angle range filter and set up theta (horizontal) start -90°, theta stop +90°, phi (vertical) start -90°, phi stop +90°, beam increment 1

docs.title: Set Port Configuration [sWN PortConfiguration]
docs.text:
Configuration of the given ports. Telegram structure represents the configuration of 1 port.

If the device has multiple ports, use the same structure.

docs.title: SOPASair Walkthrough
docs.text: This page describes the picoScan100 web interface and the settings in each view. Use it to commission the sensor before you automate the configuration through the API. To try the interface without a device, open it in the Virtual Sensor Lab.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Choose the scan configuration and the core measurement behavior. Resolution, frequency, and range trade off against each other.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

The live scan on the left updates as you change the configuration, which is the quickest way to judge a setting.

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text:
Basic Settings controls the scan configuration used by the sensor. The settings are shown on the right; the live scan on the left shows the effect of the selected frequency, angular resolution, and other settings immediately. Use this view to check coverage and measurement behavior while commissioning.

Coordinate System

The device coordinate system uses one point as the origin and reference for all laser beams and distance measurements. With no translation into a world coordinate system, this point is also the world origin.

The horizontal beam angle is theta (θ). A beam at θ = 0° points along the middle of the sensor's main viewing direction, making the scan symmetric around the X axis. The vertical elevation angle is phi (φ) and is measured from the X/Y plane. For a single-plane picoScan, φ = 0° when the sensor is ideally mounted.

Horizontal beam angle theta.

Vertical beam angle phi.

Measurement data is always output in the device coordinate system. Transform it into a world or application frame on the receiving system after accounting for the sensor's mounting position and orientation. See 3D point clouds with 2D LiDARs for an example coordinate transform.

Date and system time

The time base can be set using various methods:

  • Explicitly setting the date and time
  • Transferring the time from the computer used
  • Via an external NTP server (Network Time Protocol) that is accessible in the network. The technology uses UDP on port 123. This setting is recommended to ensure a correct time stamp in the detection history or error entries.
  • Via an external PTP (Precision Time Protocol) master that is accessible in the network. The technology uses UDP on ports 319 and 320. This setting is recommended for precise synchronization requirements (e.g. between several devices).

Dynamic Sensing Profiles

LiDAR applications often need different sensor characteristics at different times. An AMR may need the shortest response time in busy areas, a large scanning range and good angular resolution in a warehouse, and the highest close-range angular resolution while docking. Higher angular resolution requires a lower scanning frequency, so choose the priority for each application.

Dynamic Sensing Profiles allow the scan's core parameters to be changed during operation without restarting the sensor. The Scan Data Configuration function allows fast switching between profiles:

Basic Settings: profile, frequency, angular resolution, and typical use.

Profile Frequency Angular resolution Typical use 1 15 Hz 0.5° Object detection with large scanning ranges 2 15 Hz 0.33° TiM series retrofit 3 20 Hz 0.1° Fine positioning or environment maps 4 20 Hz 0.25° Low-noise measurements; recommended for LiDAR-LOC 5 25 Hz 0.25° LMS100 series retrofit 6 30 Hz 0.1° Fine positioning or environment maps 7 40 Hz 0.25° Fast object detection at a large scanning range 8 50 Hz 0.25° Very fast object detection 9 15 Hz 0.05° Highest angular resolution for static measurements 10 40 Hz 0.125° High angular resolution and high scan rate 11 15 Hz 1° TiM series retrofit

Available profiles depend on the device variant and license; see Licenses.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
Clean up the scan before it leaves the sensor by suppressing extra echoes, artifacts and airborne particles.

Example filter settings in the picoScan100 web interface. Select parameters according to the requirements of each application.

If present, the filters are applied in the following order:

  1. Fog filter
  2. Echo filter
  3. Particle filter
  4. Moving average filter
  5. Filters for data reduction and the region of interest filter

For detailed behavior and examples, see Filter details.

docs.title: Inertial Measuring Unit (IMU)
docs.text:
Use the IMU view to inspect the sensor's current orientation and acceleration.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

The IMU view displays the yaw, pitch, and roll angles in degrees, together with the measured acceleration on the X, Y, and Z axes in meters per second squared. The orientation indicator provides a visual representation of the current sensor position.

Use these values as a guide when checking the sensor installation or interpreting the scan coordinate system.

docs.title: Contamination Indication
docs.text:
Monitor the optics cover for dirt and get a warning before measurement quality drops.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

The contamination status provides a live reading of Clean, Minor, Heavy, or Blocked. The segment wheel identifies where contamination is accumulating around the optics cover. Configure whether contamination triggers a warning, an error, or both, and adjust the sensitivity and outputs for the environment.

docs.title: Connection Options
docs.text:
Give the sensor its permanent Ethernet identity so it fits your network.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

Choose static addressing to enter a fixed IP address, or DHCP to have a server assign the address automatically, according to your application and network requirements. The IP address must be unique on your network. The subnet mask defines which addresses are local, for example 255.255.255.0, and the default gateway provides access to other subnets. The MAC address and calculated speed are read-only values for reference and firewall rules.

  1. Set the addressing mode to Static.
  2. Enter the IP, subnet mask, and gateway for your network.
  3. Press Apply.
  4. Reconnect the browser at the new address.

Pressing Apply drops your current browser connection.

docs.title: Inputs and Outputs
docs.text:
Configure the multifunction I/O ports and map field-evaluation results and device states to physical outputs.

Live capture from a picoScan100's web interface.

Set each port as an input or an output and give it a name. Bind an output to a source, such as a field-evaluation result or a device state. Configure the logic (HIGH or LOW active), inversion, restart behavior, and status log. The right panel shows the live status and counters for every port.

I/O is a simple way to connect a PLC when you do not want to parse the data stream.
